snap.notes:
The Snap stub no longer reads as a tied-off sack; at the game camera it reads as a cleaved stone shaft end. Commit 4242d0d30 is pushed.

What changed: a new helper, sheared_break, in art/blender/maps/landmarks_art2.py replaces the broken_drum call for snap_stub only. broken_drum and shaft_drum are untouched, and only snap_stub.glb changed under art/out.

Design:
- A flat-ish shear, long on the west and low down, tilted to the sky.
- Six Voronoi plates in raw stone, with no vertex fan. The plates are unchamfered, because chamfers shaded them into cobbles.
- The skin ends just behind the plates, so the end reads as one solid stone.
- Four unequal loose shards sit at the short east foot.

Rebuild 1 was rejected: its deep sawtooth over cobbles read as a toothed maw. Rebuild 2 is the one shipped, and it used up the allowance of 2.

Weak points I saw when looking at it:
1. Faint hood or mask read at 2x on the north stub. The arched tear above a flat central plate, with a lower plate like a nose, can suggest a hood or mask if you look for it. At 1:1 in play I read it as faceted rock. It lies on its side and is seen from above, so I did not treat it as a sensitivity blocker, but owner_rulings.md was not checked for it and the lead should look at the A/B.
2. The north stub's end silhouette is still fairly blunt. The jagged read comes from the cracks, the tear and the shards more than from the outline. The south twin's outline is properly jagged.
3. Raw plates and needle skin are nearly the same value at the game camera, because the existing materials were kept. The read depends on cracks and facets, not on colour contrast.
4. Scatter props are not part of this asset. src/render/terrain.ts raycasts needle fragments onto upward-facing stub faces, so changing the mesh moved them, deterministically. On the north stub a needle_drum now sits half-sunk on a plate ledge and reads a little like a round socket. A slab prop also sits on the south twin. I left src alone.

Not done:
- Low quality was not captured; only High at 1080p was.
- No timing gate was run, and triangles dropped by 3.
- GE_audit.md still says the stubs were not rebuilt; it is left as the record of that pass.

I did not start it, so I did not kill it. I waited about 10 minutes until it exited by itself at 20:53 and started the gates after that. Nothing new from it appeared during my run.

It read 3533 MB in the rift match against the 3000 MB bar (ruling 20), 2973 MB in bridge, and 2479 MB at Home after rift against the 2500 MB bar, all on the Ultra preset with SMAA. It peaked 2 s into the rift match. The default preset is High, which this run did not read. The Performance section should re-measure this idle, including --preset ultra. Wip sync 20aaa35ba committed MsaaRenderPass, MSAA_ULTRA_SAMPLES = 0 and PostChain.setMsaaSamples in src/render/post.ts, and --preset in probe_match_memory.mjs. Every tier now builds through MsaaRenderPass. By code reading, 0 samples takes the plain RenderPass path and allocates nothing, but no pixel A/B or verify pass has confirmed that. GFX_verify 2's zero-pixel result predates this change. I made no source change and did not resolve it.

verify.notes: VERDICT: NOT CLEAN. 2 fails carry the weight: match_memory (blocker, RIFT as second match 3433-3461 MB against 3000, a plateau over the bar for the full 5 minutes) and audio_mix (major, probe hangs 3 of 3, context clock frozen). match_leave_journey is also a fail (2 of 3 runs). Blockers not measured: perf_realtime (92.1, 96.9, 95.6 %, all under 99, all busy), perf_gpubound_tail (58.5, 56.6, 57.5, 60 fps, all busy), e2e_all and e2e_flow (function passes, load clause missed). Also not measured: audio_sync, ge1_cost. Load: across the 5.5 hours the machine read about 2.2-3.8 even between runs, and a Chrome run pushes it over 3 (peaks 4-5.8). Top CPU at rest: booted iOS Simulator runtime processes (pids 26344, 26305, about 12-25 % each, left alone as instructed), diagnosticd, coreaudiod, sysmond, and at times TGOnDeviceInferenceProviderService, runningboardd and proactiveeventtrackerd. Timing gates that need a clean load<3 window are not reachable until that eases. How this was measured, which departs from the brief: the previous step's queue driver was still running when I started (pid 48158, orphaned, already running perf_prod). I did not kill a process I had not started and running alongside it would have spoiled both, so I let it finish (21:18-00:18) and read its raw logs, ignoring the claims. Names fw_final_idle_* are its output. Names fw_final_vfy_* are my own later runs of match memory, gpubound, calibrate, input latency, audio sync, e2e all, realtime, audio mix and lisvel seed 16. Gates with only fw_final_idle_* evidence were run once, by that driver, under the exact commands, not repeated by me. Things I ended or added: I ended my own stuck audio_mix rerun at 20 min, and my scratch diagnostic at 200 s. The driver's first audio_mix was killed by its own 1200 s limit. The diagnostic was a scratchpad copy of the probe with one log line; nothing under _harness was edited. Harness gap: perf_1080 --calibrate-only prints GATE PASS with no note at load 3.43->3.63. perf_1080 prints PASS inside a busy gpubound row. Tracked reports rewritten by runs were restored by the driver, with copies in _harness/_reports/fw_final_idle_snap and fw_final_vfy_snap.
